1. The present appeal is filed by the petitioner/claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 26.08.2021 passed in MVC No.902/2018 by the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ranebennur.
2. Brief facts, leading to rise the filing of this appeal are as follows:
3. On 01.10.2017, the deceased Gangamma and the petitioner were returning to their native place in a Cruiser vehicle bearing registration No.KA-27/B-2699 as authorized passengers.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ranebennur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
A lorry bearing registration No.KA- 13/8233 was parked in the middle of the road after loading eucalyptus poles,
without giving any indication or warning signal.
At that time, there was drizzling rain and the atmosphere was cloudy.
Due to poor visibility, the driver of the cruiser could not notice the parked lorry.
Consequently, the driver of the cruiser lost control over the vehicle, and dashed against the rear portion of the lorry, resulting in the NC: 2026:KHC-D:3631 HC-KAR accident.
As a result of the accident, Gangamma sustained grievous injuries, and succumbed to the injuries, and the petitioner also sustained grievous injuries.
The petitioner filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act (for short, 'the MV Act') seeking compensation.
The legal heirs of deceased Gangamma also filed a claim petition in MVC No.901/2018.
Both the claim petitions were clubbed together, and tried jointly.
4. As per the tribunal records, respondent No.1 is the owner of the lorry, respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said lorry, and respondent No.3 is the owner of the cruiser vehicle.
5. A Notice was issued to respondent No.1.
Despite service of notice, he remained unrepresented and was placed ex parte before the tribunal.
6. Respondent - the Insurance Company - filed its statement of objections denying the averments made in the claim petition and contended that there was a violation of policy conditions.

Hence, it contended that it is not liable to pay the compensation as claimed by the petitioner and NC:
2026:KHC-D:3631 HC-KAR accordingly, prayed for dismissal of the claim petition against it.
7.

Respondent - owner of the cruiser filed a statement of objections denying the averments made in the claim petition and contended that the owner or driver of the cruiser vehicle is not liable to pay Channabasappa S/O Basappa vs Uma W/O Basavaraj on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91851305/
3 compensation as claimed by the petitioners.

entities.text: Channabasappa S/O Basappa vs Uma W/O Basavaraj
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, prays to dismiss the claim petition.
8. The Tribunal clubbed the claim petitions, and framed separate issues for consideration.
9. The petitioner in MVC No.902/2018 was examined as PW-2, and the doctor was examined as PW-4.
In MVC No.901/2018, petitioner No.1 was examined as PW- 1 and the other witness was examined as PW-3.

In all, 17 documents were marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P17.
10.

In rebuttal, the officer of insurance company was examined as RW-1, and one document was marked as Ex.R1.
11.

After assessing the oral and documentary evidence on record, the Tribunal partly allowed the claim NC: 2026:KHC-D:3631 HC-KAR petition and awarded a compensation of Rs.5,42,308/- with interest at the rate of 7% p.a. from the date of petition till its payment.
12. In MVC No.902/2018, the petitioner, being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, has filed the present Miscellaneous First Appeal.

13. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the petitioner, and the learned counsel for the insurance company.
14.

The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the accident is of 2017 and the Tribunal ought to have assessed the notional income at Rs.10,250/- per month, as per the schedule issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
However, the Tribunal assessed the income at Rs.10,000/-, which is on the lower side.
15. He further submits that to prove the disability, the petitioner examined the doctor who has opined that the petitioner suffered 99.6% permanent physical disability.
However, the Tribunal assessed the disability at 10%, which NC: 2026:KHC-D:3631 HC-KAR is on the lower side.
He further submits that the compensation awarded under the other heads is also inadequate.
Hence, on these grounds he prays to allow the appeal.

16. Per contra, the learned counsel for the insurance company submits that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and does not call for any interference at the hands of this Court.
Hence, he prays to dismiss the appeal.

17. Perused the records, and considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties.
18.
The point that would arise for consideration regarding to the quantum of compensation.
19. There is no dispute regarding the occurrence of the accident.
The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the drivers of both the vehicles.
It is also on record that the driver of the lorry had parked the vehicle in the middle of the road without giving any signal.
Therefore, both the drivers contributed to the cause of the accident.

Channabasappa S/O Basappa vs Uma W/O Basavaraj on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91851305/
4 NC: 2026:KHC-D:3631 HC-KAR 20.
The charge sheet has been filed against the drivers of both the vehicles and the same is marked as Ex.P8.
Hence, the Tribunal was justified in recording a finding that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the drivers of both vehicles.

Regarding quantum of compensation:
21.
The petitioner contended that he is an agriculturist earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
However, to substantiate the said claim, no documentary evidence has been produced.

In the absence of proof of income, this Court assesses the notional income at Rs.10,250/- per month as per the schedule issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, since the accident occurred year 2017.

22. The petitioner was aged about 55 years at the time of the accident, and the applicable multiplier for the said age group is '11', as per the principles laid down in the case of Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation Limited reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121.

entities.text: Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation Limited reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: NC: 2026:KHC-D:3631 HC-KAR 23.
The petitioner examined the doctor i.e., P.W.4 who deposed that the petitioner has suffered 99.6% permanent disability.

If the petitioner had really suffered such a high percentage of disability,
he would have been completely bedridden.
On the contrary, the appellant appeared before the tribunal and gave evidence, which indicates that the disability assessed by the doctor appears to be exaggerated.
24. The Tribunal assessed the disability at 10%, which appears to be on the lower side.
Considering the overall evidence on record, this Court reassesses the disability at 15%.

25. Accordingly, the compensation is reassessed under the following heads:
Compensation Particulars amount in (Rs.) Pain and sufferings 50,000/-
Loss of dependency (Rs.10,250 x 12 x 2,02,950/-
 11 x 15%)
 Medical Expenses 3,61,808/-
Diet, food and nourishment charges 30,000/-
- 10 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:3631 HC-KAR Loss of income during laid-up period 30,750/-
Channabasappa S/O Basappa vs Uma W/O Basavaraj on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91851305/
5  Loss of amenities 30,000/-
 Total 7,05,508/-
 Compensation awarded by the Tribunal 5,42,308/-
 Enhanced compensation 1,63,200/-
 26.
Thus, the petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.7,05,508/- as against Rs.5,42,308/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled to an enhanced compensation of Rs.1,63,200/- for the forgoing the point is answered accordingly.
27. In view of the above discussion, I proceed to pass the following order.
ORDER (i) This Miscellaneous First Appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The impugned judgment and award  passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.902/2018 is hereby modified.

(iii) The appellant is entitled to an  enhanced compensation of  Rs.1,63,200/-, in addition to the compensation awarded by the Tribunal,
- 11 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:3631 HC-KAR with interest at the rate of 7% percent per annum from the date of the petition till its realisation.
(iv) Insofar as liability is concerned, the Tribunal has fastened 50% liability on Respondent No.2-Shriram General Insurance Co. Ltd. and 50% liability on respondent No.3, the owner of the cruiser vehicle.
The same is maintained.
